name: Progression to Zombie
description: Progression to Zombie from New York is a reset when the opponent recovers the inside hand. Pummel it back to the mat before restoring arm isolation and the knee hug.
summary: Zombie is the hand-clearing pummel from Mission Control into New York; it is needed again only if the opponent has recovered the arm inside.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Completed New York already contains the result of the Zombie pummel. First recognize a lost arm isolation and re-establish Mission Control rather than treating Zombie as a later static lockdown.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): What has to be lost before New York needs Zombie again?
flashcards.answer: Zombie normally creates New York. A renewed attempt requires the opponent to have recovered the hand or forearm inside.

plausible: Only free foot's contact with mat
Second leg's closure behind the head

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): What holds posture while you re-pummel?
flashcards.answer: Keep posture broken with a supported high leg so the free arm can work on the hand opening.
flashcards.answer_line: Supported high leg held by one hand

plausible: Both hands pull wrist with leg down
High ankle held, knee drifting back

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): Where does Eddy begin against a tight elbow clamp?
flashcards.answer: The hand-first version seeks the weaker opening under the hand rather than prying directly beneath the clamped elbow.

plausible: At the tight underside of the elbow
Over the top of their wrist
trap: Around the outside of their forearm

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): How should the cleared hand travel?
flashcards.answer: The pummel moves the wrist and forearm through available space so the inside frame becomes an outside arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Guide hand and forearm out to mat

plausible: Back onto the opponent's own chest
Straight up, forearm stays inside

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): What locks in the pummel's positional gain?
flashcards.answer: The hand reaching the mat is followed by arm coverage and knee support so the opponent cannot easily re-pummel inside.
flashcards.answer_line: Cover arm and hug the raised knee

plausible: Arm left open as both grips change
Drop high leg before covering arm

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): Their hand circles back inside; what was missing?
flashcards.answer: The pummel must close the return path with the arm wrap and supported knee; lifting the hand alone can leave it recoverable.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm coverage as the knee hug closed

plausible: Higher ankle grip; elbow uncovered
Tighter head pull with knee away

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): Their inside frames stay intact; what is a sound reset?
flashcards.answer: A blocked hand path calls for retaining guard and waiting for another opening, rather than forcing the elbow clamp.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep guard; reopen space by the hand

plausible: Abandon guard; pull elbow outward
Circle both arms behind their back
trap: Dig under elbow with hand gap shut

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): What configuration confirms the pummel succeeded?
flashcards.answer: The success checkpoint is New York arm isolation supported by the high leg; Zombie is the action that creates it.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand on mat; arm wrapped; knee hug

plausible: Both forearms inside on your chest
Hand on mat; elbow across your chest
trap: Wrist out; knee floats off the arm

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): Posture breaks free during the pummel; what comes first?
flashcards.answer: Recover guard structure when the high connection fails, rather than continuing to chase the arm while the torso gap opens.

plausible: Neck-clearing grip before knee space
Two-hand wrist pull, knees outside
trap: New ankle grip before near knee in

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (bottom): Which support should a first pummel drill preserve?
flashcards.answer: Practice the hand-clearing path with the high knee supported and posture controlled before adding resistance or follow-up attacks.
flashcards.answer_line: High knee near torso as hand clears

plausible: Foot high while knee drifts away
Opponent stays upright throughout
trap: Knee forward, support hand on wrist

defender.name: Progression to Zombie Defender
defender.description: Progression to Zombie (defender): Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Completed New York already contains the result of the Zombie pummel. First recognize a lost arm isolation and re-establish Mission Control rather than treating Zombie as a later static lockdown.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The early escape keeps the elbow inside and denies the knee hug. Treat the renewed arm isolation as a submission setup once it closes, and open the connection safely instead of twisting the trapped shoulder.

Keep elbow and hand connected: Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
Notice the pummel early: The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.
Recover without yanking: Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught.
Rebuild posture gradually: Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control.
Respect the high guard: Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (top): What should you retain after regaining your inside hand?
flashcards.answer: Retain the recovered frame so the guard player cannot immediately clear the hand out again.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside elbow with a forearm frame

plausible: Hand on mat outside, elbow wide
Long reach behind their far shoulder
trap: Wrist at chest, elbow outside thigh

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (top): Your hand starts inside; how do you finish recovering that arm?
flashcards.answer: Coordinated arm recovery prevents the wrist being left exposed while the elbow remains trapped outside.
flashcards.answer_line: Return elbow to ribs with the hand

plausible: Palm on chest; elbow stays outside
Elbow forward toward their head
trap: Repost your hand wide for balance

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (top): When should you react to the pummeling hand?
flashcards.answer: The under-hand entry is an early cue to recover inside position before the knee hug secures the arm outside.
flashcards.answer_line: As their hand starts beneath yours

plausible: After knee hug fully fixes elbow
Only once high leg lowers fully
trap: When your hand reaches the outer mat

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (top): How can a caught elbow return to your side?
flashcards.answer: Draw the elbow beside the ribs when the shoulder has room; stop if the arm is already loaded.
flashcards.answer_line: Through slack in the opened high leg

plausible: Pull harder against a fixed knee hug
Extend your elbow against the leg
trap: Pull wrist in before shoulder frees

flashcards.question: Progression to Zombie (top): What must change before a strong posture recovery?
flashcards.answer: Recover chest height only after the arm can move and the high leg no longer fixes the neck and shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm and high leg release upper body

plausible: Only turn your palm to face upward
Only move the free knee wider
trap: Wrist free; high thigh still linked
